LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS PHONETIC AWARENESS INTONATION CHUNKING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.8: Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is correct pronunciation important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli
2. appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS PHONETIC AWARENESS INTONATION CHUNKING
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS PHONETIC AWARENESS INTONATION CHUNKING
Study Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking” in your own words using one local example. (skill: recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking. (skill: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is correct pronunciation important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological awareness Phonetic awareness Intonation Chunking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise letter sounds in words from audio stimuli.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
